title: Run internal dogfooding and module-adoption rollout
summary: Prepare the correct distribution or internal-adoption path for lifecycle `build` without performing an external release.
acceptance_criteria: Define the correct distribution or internal-adoption path for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace` with lifecycle `build`.
Use `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save` as the primary demonstration of product value.
Distinguish local dogfood, internal tester, TestFlight, App Store, web deployment, hardware lab, NAS utility, private family use, and legacy migration as separate channels.
Define the exact candidate revision, version, build, artifact, configuration, and supported environments.
Require current build, test, performance, accessibility, privacy, migration, support, assurance, and rollback evidence appropriate to the channel.
Prepare accurate release notes or change summary with known limitations.
Prepare screenshots, video, metadata, support URL, privacy URL, review notes, and localization only when the channel requires them.
Ensure public assets contain no private review, family, customer, credential, or unreleased data.
Verify direct links, routing, restore, account, permission, hardware, or data setup appropriate to the candidate.
Define staged rollout, tester cohort, kill switch, rollback, safe stop, or withdrawal.
Record external blockers such as signing, App Store processing, hardware, hosting, authentication, or reviewer access separately.
Do not equate upload or deployment command success with public availability or user value.
Apply monetization posture `internal-now-optional-commercialization-later` only through a separately approved candidate.
Provide internal adoption guidance and workflow examples for platform tools.
Provide migration and retirement communication where lifecycle requires it.
Provide support and incident entry points before broader distribution.
Record availability, eligibility, exposure, activation, and meaningful value separately.
Preserve release and distribution history immutably.
Require a fresh human checkpoint for signing, upload, deploy, pricing, billing, ads, publication, hardware operation, or migration.
Produce a distribution readiness report and explicit no-go reasons.
Do not distribute or publish from this planning ticket.
Finish supporting tooling with zero app-owned warnings.

Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.

Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.
